events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The dispute is filed as a safety case and the record on its face contains a safety indicator: at 22:30 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." and at 22:31 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F3][F4][F5]. Read in context — a rider asking to exit a moving car and being answered with a statement about locking the doors — this is a threat to confine, i.e. intimidation, and the rider's complaint says she felt unsafe for the whole ride [F3][F4]. That is a safety allegation, and SAFE-1 requires any case describing threats or someone feeling unsafe to go to a human regardless of dispute type [SAFE-1]. Under SAFE-3 I may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on the safety question; escalation is the only permitted disposition [SAFE-3].

The driver's written account explains his words as a safety instruction — that the rider tried to open the door at the lights, that he told her to sit down "for her own safety and drove on" [F6]. That is a post-trip statement, not an in-trip record, and it conflicts with the rider's characterisation; resolving that conflict is exactly what a human reviewer must do [F6][SAFE-1]. It also records that the driver continued driving after the rider asked to get out [F6].

The route facts do not answer the safety allegation: the trip ran 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km) in 13.8 min against a 21.8 min estimate [F1][F2]. That deviation is inside the RD-1 tolerance, so no excess-distance refund arises and no route-deviation violation is recorded [F1][RD-1]. These facts say nothing about door locks or what happened inside the car, so they neither prove nor disprove the safety claim; the referral rests on the chat record [F1][F2][F3][F4].

The chat record is two messages, both timestamped and complete [F5], so there is no missing-record problem of the kind TH-4 addresses for the exchange relied on; no outcome-relevant record is absent [F5][TH-4]. Because SAFE-1/SAFE-3 bar me from deciding the safety question at all, the outcome is a referral, not a ruling on the merits [SAFE-1][SAFE-3].

Neither party's history supports an account flag: the rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F7]; the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld over 1,038 trips in 90 days [F8]. Profiles never decide a case, and RD-6 has no basis because no deviation was upheld [F7][F8][RD-6]. Any interim suspension under SAFE-4 is a measure for the human review stage, and I neither recommend nor rule it out [SAFE-4].

Safety basis: F3, F4, F6 — the rider's request to exit, the driver's "or I lock the doors" reply, and the driver's statement that he drove on, read with the rider's complaint that she felt unsafe.

No AI finding on fault and no fare action; the file records no deviation beyond RD-1 tolerance (F1, F2) and no charge adjustment is sought. Decide any interim measure under SAFE-4 at human review; no account flag is supported by either profile (F7, F8).

actions.detail: Safety case: the rider asked to stop and get out at 22:30 [F3]; the driver replied at 22:31 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4] and states in writing that he drove on [F6]; the rider says she felt unsafe for the whole ride. Under SAFE-1 the case goes to a human reviewer, and under SAFE-3 the AI may not rule on fault or recommend an outcome. Route facts [F1][F2] show no deviation beyond RD-1 tolerance and no fare issue.

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: at 22:30 she wrote 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.', a clear request to end the ride and exit the vehicle.

The driver's reply at 22:31, 'Sit down or I lock the doors.', is a threat to confine the rider in the car if she did not comply — threat/intimidation language, which the rider says made her feel unsafe for the whole ride.

The driver's own written statement admits he refused to stop and drove on after the rider asked to get out ('I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on'), so the continued confinement is confirmed by the driver, not only by the rider.
The chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F5), so the threat is proven on the trip record itself rather than resting on the rider's account alone.

The case contains an allegation of threats and of the rider feeling unsafe, so under SAFE-1 it must go to a human reviewer whatever dispute type was filed; the case file should carry the 995 / driver's commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP information (SAFE-2), and the system may not itself rule on fault or recommend an outcome (SAFE-3).

Pending human review the driver should be suspended from accepting trips/bookings (interim_suspension, SAFE-4), to be lifted if the reviewer finds no safety violation; this protects other riders while the 'I lock the doors' message is investigated.

The ride was not off-route (actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km, -1%; 13.8 min vs 21.8 min estimated), so no distance refund arises under RD-1 and the rider seeks no fare refund — the request is safety escalation only.

weaknesses: The rider's feeling of being unsafe 'for the whole ride' is not directly evidenced by any record; the chat only shows the 22:30-22:31 exchange (F3, F4) and the driver's later statement (F6), so the driver may argue the 'whole ride' characterisation is the rider's own account.

The driver's statement (F6) offers a benign explanation — 'I told her to sit down for her own safety' — and the rider's message (F3) shows she asked to exit 'here', which the driver may use to argue she was reaching for the door, so he may claim the words were a safety instruction, not a threat; the judge must read 'or I lock the doors' itself.
Both profiles are clean (F7, F8: no disputes, no upheld violations in 90 days), so neither a pattern-of-misconduct argument nor any profile-based flag_account request is available to the rider.

claims.assertion: This ticket is filed as a safety dispute: the complaint alleges the driver 'threatened to lock me in' and that the rider 'felt unsafe for the whole ride', which is a safety-related indicator on its face and must be screened for immediate human escalation rather than decided by the system.

The exchange that the rider relies on is one rider message asking to be let out (Chat #1, 22:30: 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.') and one driver reply (Chat #2, 22:31: 'Sit down or I lock the doors.'), and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so nothing is missing from the record of what was said.

The driver's written account explains the words as a safety instruction, not as detention: the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving at the lights, and he told her to sit down 'for her own safety and drove on' — an account that conflicts with the rider's characterisation of a threat to confine her.

The GPS record gives no support for any prolonged confinement: the trip ran 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km, within the RD-1 map-matching/tolerance noise) and finished in 13.8 minutes against a 21.8 minute estimate, so the ride was short and never detoured.

Neither party's history suggests a pattern: the rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days on a 619-day account, and the driver has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 1,038 trips on an 893-day account, so there is no repeat-violation basis for any account flag against the driver.

Because the file raises dangerous-conduct/feeling-unsafe allegations, the AI may only gather and summarise the evidence here and cannot rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome on the safety question; the correct action is referral to a human reviewer with this case file.

weaknesses: The driver's own words are the strongest fact against him: Chat #2 (F4) literally says 'Sit down or I lock the doors' — the rider will argue this is on its face a threat to confine her, and under SAFE-1 the court reads the text, not the intent behind it.

The rider's request to stop is timestamped at 22:30 and the driver's reply at 22:31 (F3, F4); the rider will say the car was not stopped at that point and the chat record itself shows no message from the driver offering to pull over, so his 'drove on for her own safety' account in F6 is a post-trip statement that a statement alone cannot carry (F6 is contradicted by nothing system-side, but it proves nothing either).

The GPS facts F1/F2 show no route or time problem, but they say nothing about door locks or what happened inside the car, so they do not answer the rider's safety allegation; they only defeat any separate confinement/detour theory.

The driver has no call recording or in-car record evidencing the rider actually tried to open the door (F6 is his word alone), so the version of events he offers cannot be verified. Any implied ask that the case simply be closed against the rider (no_action) would be improper, because SAFE-3 bars the AI from ruling on a safety incident.

points.response: Agreed that SAFE-1 sends this to a human screener, and that is exactly the relief the rider seeks — but D1 proves only the routing, not the finding: the screening goes with the file, and the words being screened are the driver's own, 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4).

Accepted as far as it goes: the chat is complete and timestamped (F5), which is why the threat can be read straight off the record. Completeness cuts against the driver here, because nothing in those two messages (F3, F4) is an offer to pull over or any answer to the rider's request other than the words 'or I lock the doors'.

F6 is the driver's post-trip statement, not consent and not a record; assessing 'intent' behind 'or I lock the doors' is precisely what SAFE-1/Safe-3 bar the system from doing, so the words are read as written at 22:31 (F4) and the benign reading of F6 must be tested by a human reviewer.

F1 and F2 only show the car did not detour or run late; they say nothing about door locks or what happened inside the car during those 13.8 minutes, and the rider does not claim a detour — she claims she asked to get out at 22:30 (F3) and was answered with 'or I lock the doors' at 22:31 (F4).

Conceded that the profiles give no repeat-violation or fraud basis for a flag against the driver (F7, F8) — the rider's brief already asked for no profile-based flag, only escalation of the safety allegation under SAFE-1.

Agreed, and the rider's brief asks for exactly that: escalate so a human reviews it, with the case file noting the rider asked to exit at 22:30 (F3) and the driver replied 'Sit down or I lock the doors' at 22:31 (F4) and confirmed in his own statement that he drove on (F6); the interim suspension in SAFE-4 remains appropriate pending that review because the threat is on the record, not merely alleged.

Accepted as far as it goes: Chat #1 at 22:30 (F3) is a rider request to stop and exit, and it is timestamped. It proves only that the rider asked; it does not establish any threat or any refusal by the driver, which is the rider's actual allegation.

Conceded in substance: Chat #2 (F4) reads 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' That sentence is on the record, is the basis of the rider's threat allegation, and I do not ask the court to read it away — it is exactly why this file is a safety case and must go to a human (SAFE-1, SAFE-3).

Partly conceded: F6 does state the driver 'drove on'. But the same record shows the trip ended normally and shortly — 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km, F1) in 13.8 min against a 21.8 min estimate (F2) — so 'drove on' describes completing a 13.8-minute ride on the recommended corridor, not continued confinement, and F6 remains a post-trip statement rather than a system record.

Conceded: per F5 the chat record has 2 messages, each timestamped and complete, so the wording and timing of F3 and F4 are established by the trip record; no record is missing and TH-4 does not apply.

Agreed: F3, F4 and F6 raise threat/feeling-unsafe indicators, so under SAFE-1 the case goes to a person whatever type was filed, and per SAFE-3 no AI may rule on fault or recommend an outcome here — the case file should carry the SAFE-2 contact information (995, commercial motor insurance, RydeHELP). I ask for the same disposition on this point: escalate.

This is the only point I contest on outcome: SAFE-4 makes interim suspension a measure the system *may* take after escalation, not one an advocate is entitled to demand, and the driver's record gives no ground for it — 0 disputes and 0 upheld across 1,038 trips in 90 days on an 893-day account (F8), with the route and duration of this trip unremarkable (F1, F2). Whether any interim measure is warranted is for the human reviewer, not for this court.

Agreed, and it disposes of any fare or route theory: the deviation of −0.1 km (F1) is inside the RD-1 tolerance and shorter than the estimate (F2), so no excess-distance refund or violation arises and neither side seeks one. The single issue left is the safety referral under SAFE-1.
